done.why: I had just reached the Gallery and tried to take the painting when the world told me I'd used all 30 turns. I was actually still interested at that point — the 'Back soon -- The Management' note and the stolen-paintings gallery had just started making this feel different from the Zork I half-remember — so I'd have kept going a bit.

about: A white house in a field with a cellar underneath that opens into caves: a troll, a maze, a chasm, an art gallery. It's the Zork opening, but someone has been editing the underground — passages are 'not finished' with notes pinned up by 'The Management', like the place is under construction or being renovated while you walk through it. Treasure-hunting under a house that's quietly being rebuilt around you.

moments.note: Climbing in through the window and landing in the kitchen with the pepper sack — quick, concrete, got me inside in six moves.
Trap door slams and someone bars it behind me. Who? Nice little jolt.
Troll fight is dice: miss, knocked to knees, 'still recovering', five swings. It's a lot of typing the same line.
'It's curtains for the troll as your sword removes his head.' Earned.
East passage 'has not been finished. Back soon. -- The Management.' First sign this isn't plain Zork. Funny, and made me want to know what else was changed.
Maze: 'Maze' and nothing else when I moved. Two steps in and I was already thinking about quitting it.
Going east from the maze dumped me straight back in the Troll Room. Either lucky or the maze is short now.
'Your load is too heavy' for the painting on the very last turn, then the cap hit. Should've dropped the axe.

wished: Ask or find out who barred the trap door behind me — the world made a point of it and then dropped it.
Push past or examine the 'unfinished' east passage; a note from The Management begs to be investigated and I couldn't.
Have the maze tell me something — anything — on a move, instead of just 'Maze'.
A warning before the last turn so I could drop the axe and actually take the painting.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: The first moment I felt watched. Someone is in the house.

lines.line: It's curtains for the troll as your sword removes his head.
lines.why: The payoff after four dud swings; made the fight feel worth it.

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. A note is pinned to the rock: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: This is where the world stopped being a memory and became its own thing. Dry, odd, and the single most interesting line I read.

lines.line: Most of the paintings have been stolen by vandals with exceptional taste.
lines.why: Made me grin and gave me a goal: be the last vandal.

fun.why: The first fifteen turns moved fast and the troll beheading and the Management note were genuinely fun. The repetitive fight and the blank maze dragged, and the turn cap landed right as I got a goal.

engagement.why: I stayed in because each room led somewhere quickly; the barred trap door and the Management note hooked me. The maze (two moves of 'Maze') nearly lost me.

difficulty.why: Nothing stopped me except luck in the troll fight and my own overloaded inventory at the end. The maze spat me out after two moves.

interestingness.why: The 'unfinished passage' with a note from The Management, and the gallery's vandals 'with exceptional taste', are a tone I wanted more of. Only two such moments in 30 turns though.

prose.why: Mostly clipped, functional room text. The good lines are good — the troll's death, the vandals, the Management note — but moving in the maze returned a single word.
